alexandria_desc.en: Once the beacon of the Mediterranean, Alexandria thrives as a crossroads of trade and scholarship. Its lighthouse and library once proclaimed a city where cultures and empires converged.
alexandria_desc.uk: Александрія, колись відома своїм грандіозним маяком і бібліотекою, знаходиться на межі різних цивілізацій і культур. За рахунок цього вона й досі залишається важливим торговельним і освітнім центром Середземномор'я.

amasya_desc.en: Nestled in a deep gorge cut by the Yeşilırmak River through the Pontic mountains, Amasya was the royal capital of the ancient kingdom of Pontus and the birthplace of the geographer Strabo, who described it in loving detail in his great work on the geography of the world. Its dramatic setting, with rock-cut royal tombs carved into the cliff faces above the river, expressed the grandeur of a Hellenistic kingdom that at its height extended its rule across much of Asia Minor. Under Byzantine, Danishmendid, Seljuk, and Mongol rule the city retained its importance as the principal center of the Pontic foothills, its deep gorge and mountain setting making it one of the most naturally defensible positions in northern Anatolia.

ancona_desc.en: Founded as a Greek colony by Syracusan exiles on the Adriatic coast, Ancona takes its name from the Greek word for elbow, describing the curved headland that shelters its harbor from the north. In the Middle Ages it grew into the most important port on the central Adriatic, its merchants trading with Byzantine Constantinople and the ports of the Levant. Despite repeated attempts by popes and emperors to bring it to heel, Ancona maintained a fierce communal independence, its harbor and its fleet the foundations of a freedom jealously guarded for centuries.

angkor_desc.en: Deep in the forests of mainland Southeast Asia, the Khmer kings of Angkor built a capital unlike any other. Begun under Suryavarman II in the early 12th century, the vast temple complex of Angkor Wat was dedicated to Vishnu and designed as an earthly image of the cosmos, its moats representing the cosmic ocean and its towers the peaks of Mount Meru. At its height the greater Angkor region was sustained by an intricate system of reservoirs and irrigation canals, making it one of the most extensive urban complexes in the pre-industrial world.

ankara_desc.en: Set on a rocky hilltop at the heart of the Anatolian plateau, Ankara was an ancient Galatian city long before the Romans made it the chief city of their province of Galatia. Its strategic position where the roads from Constantinople, the Black Sea, the Levant, and Persia all converge gave it enduring military and commercial importance, and the great temple raised by its citizens in honor of Augustus preserved inscriptions that stand among the most important surviving records of Roman history. Under the Danishmendids, the Seljuks of Rum, and the Mongols in turn, Ankara remained the key junction of the Anatolian plateau, a city whose possession signified control of the roads that crossed it.

aquila_desc.en: One of the youngest great cities of medieval Italy, L'Aquila was founded around 1254 from the union of nearly a hundred villages of the Abruzzo highlands, each said to have contributed a church, a fountain, a quarter, and a bell to the new city. Set high in the Apennines at the heart of the mountain kingdom, the city grew with remarkable speed into the capital of Abruzzo, its position and walls securing it against rival lords and the ambitions of the distant Neapolitan court. The unusual circumstances of its founding, with nearly a hundred contributing communities each maintaining a share of civic identity, gave Aquila a peculiar complexity and a fierce local pride unlike any other city in the Italian south.

athens_desc.en: Considered the cultural centre of Ancient Greece, Athens grew to be one of the mightiest city states of its time. Being at odds with Sparta, Thebes, and other states of antiquity, it slowly grew to be the dominating maritime power of the Aegean Sea. With its subjugation under the Macedonian Empire, and later on the Roman and Byzantine Empires, the city faced a major decline, and after 1204, the head of a Crusading State.
athens_desc.uk: Афіни вважалися культурним центром Стародавньої Греції і були одним із наймогутніших міст-держав свого часу. Суперничаючи зі Спартою, Фівами та іншими античними державами, Афіни поступово досягли панування в Егейському морі. Пізніше місто було завойоване спочатку Македонською, а потім Римською та Візантійською імперіями, через що прийшло в занепад. Тим не менш після 1204 року Афіни знову піднеслися, ставши столицею новоутвореної держави хрестоносців.

augsburg_desc.en: Once known as #italic Augusta Videlicum#! during the reign of the Roman Emperor Trajan, the Free Imperial City of Augsburg is one of the oldest cities in the Holy Roman Empire. At the end of the Early Middle Ages, Augsburg grew in importance as it served as showplace of one of the successful defenses against the invading Hungarians in 955. In 1276, this importance expanded even further as Augsburg received its Imperial City right from King Rudolf von Habsburg, which opened the path to a prosperous future.
augsburg_desc.uk: Відомий під назвою #italic Августа Вінделіків#! у роки правління імператора Траяна, вільне імперське місто Аугсбург вважається одним із найдавніших міст Священної Римської імперії. У 955 році місцевому гарнізону вдалося відбити напад угорських військ, внаслідок чого значення міста помітно зросло. У 1276 році король Рудольф I дарував Аугсбургу статус імперського міста, що ознаменувало новий етап у його розвитку і посприяло його подальшому процвітанню.

aviles_desc.en: Dating back to the 10th century, Avilés is a town developed along an estuary that gave it strategic importance as a port. In the nearby Castle of Gauzón, King Alfonso III of Asturias ordered the craft of the votive Victory Cross, which was covered with gold and precious stones and is now the symbol of the entire kingdom. From the 11th century onward, Avilés became a royal town, recognized for its maritime trade and the storage and distribution of salt.
aviles_desc.uk: Авілес було засновано в X столітті в гирлі однойменної річки, завдяки чому воно здобуло важливе стратегічне значення як порт. У розташованому поблизу замку Гаусон король Астурії Альфонсо III наказав виготовити Хрест перемоги — прикрашену золотом і дорогоцінним камінням реліквію, яка згодом стала символом королівства. В XI столітті Авілес отримав статус королівського міста і став одним із центрів морської торгівлі, в якому також зберігалися значні запаси солі, видобутої в інших регіонах держави.

baden_desc.en: Initially known as #italic Civitas Aurelia Aquensis#! after being founded by the Romans, this city started carrying the name 'Baden-Baden' in the early Middle Ages, lending its name to the Margraves of Baden.
baden_desc.uk: Початкове поселення на цьому місці було засновано римлянами і носило назву #italic Civitas Aurelia Aquensis#!. В епоху раннього Середньовіччя місто стало відоме як Баден, і пізніше ця назва також перейшла до Баденського дому династії Церінгенів, який почав правити цими землями.

baghdad_desc.en: Founded in 762 by the Abbasid caliph Al-Mansur on the western bank of the Tigris, Baghdad was designed from the outset to be the center of the world. Its circular plan, the legendary Round City, placed the caliph's palace and great mosque at its heart, surrounded by markets and residences radiating outward. At the height of Abbasid power it was home to over a million souls, its House of Wisdom drawing scholars from across the known world to translate, debate, and discover. The Mongol sack of 1258 shattered this golden age, but the city endured, still the greatest metropolis of the Tigris-Euphrates heartland.

barcelona_desc.en: Founded as the Roman colony of #italic Barcino#! in the 1st century BC, Barcelona grew into the capital of the County of Catalonia and, by the 12th century, the maritime engine of the Crown of Aragon. Its merchant fleet and consulates stretched from the Balearics to Sicily, and from Sardinia to the crusader ports of Greece, making it the dominant sea power of the western Mediterranean. On the slopes below its great cathedral and ancient Roman walls, the city hummed with the commerce of a maritime power that looked outward to the sea for its wealth and destiny.

belgrad_desc.en: Standing at the confluence of the Sava and Danube rivers, where the great road from Central Europe descends into the Balkans, Belgrade has been a fortified gateway since ancient times, when the Romans called it #italic Singidunum#! and stationed a legion here to guard the Danube frontier. In the Middle Ages the city passed between Bulgarians, Byzantines, and Hungarians, its hilltop fortress above the river junction making it one of the most contested strongholds in the Balkans. By the early 14th century it stood as a key prize in the struggle between the Hungarian Kingdom and the rising Serbian state, its walls watching over the rivers that divided the worlds of Latin and Orthodox Christianity.

bilbao_desc.en: Officially founded in 1300 by Diego López de Haro, Lord of Biscay, the town soon became an important hub in Northern Spain. Nestled in a narrow valley and at the start of the Nervión river estuary, the walled settlement developed a potent shipyard industry and became the main port of export to English and Flemish ports of precious Castilian Merino wool and local high quality iron ore.
bilbao_desc.uk: Більбао було засновано в 1300 році Дієго Лопесом де Аро, сеньйором Біскайї. Розташоване в гирлі річки Нервьйон, невдовзі це місто стало важливим торговельним вузлом і центром кораблебудівної промисловості в Північній Іспанії. Крім того, завдяки своїй розвиненій портовій інфраструктурі Більбао слугувало місцем, з якого купці перевозили місцеву залізну руду та кастильську мериносову вовну прямісінько в англійські та фламандські порти.

bologna_desc.en: Founded as the Etruscan city of #italic Felsina#! and later the Roman colony of #italic Bononia#!, Bologna stands at the foot of the Apennines where the Via Emilia meets the roads north to the Po valley. It is known above all for its university, established in 1088 and the oldest in the world, which drew students of law, medicine, and philosophy from every corner of Europe to its lecture halls and the shadow of its twin medieval towers. The wealth of its merchants, the authority of its bishops, and the independence of its commune made Bologna one of the most contested prizes in the politics of medieval Italy.

brescia_desc.en: Lying at the foot of the Alpine foothills where the pre-Alps descend toward the Lombard plain, Brescia was one of the great industrial cities of medieval Italy, its forges producing weapons and armor of renowned quality traded across Europe. As a free commune it was among the most vigorous members of the Lombard League, and its citizens' defiance of imperial armies became a cornerstone of the north Italian communal tradition. Caught between the great ambitions of Milan and Venice, Brescia's strategic position at the gateway to the Alpine passes and the quality of its craftsmen made it a prize that neither power would willingly surrender.

bruges_desc.en: At the height of medieval commerce, Bruges served as the great marketplace of northern Europe, where Venetian galleys, Hanseatic cogs, and Iberian caravels all discharged their cargoes. Founded on a tidal inlet linking it to the North Sea, the city's cloth halls and exchange, considered the world's first bourse, made it the financial capital of the north. From English wool to Levantine spices, the wealth of the known world flowed through its canals and counting houses.

bursa_desc.en: Nestled below the slopes of Bithynian Mount Olympus, Bursa was a prosperous Byzantine city when the Ottoman chieftain Orhan captured it in 1326 after a decade-long siege. Orhan made it the first true capital of the Ottoman state, raising mosques, caravanserais, and a covered bazaar that would define the city's character for centuries. As the western terminus of Silk Road caravans from the East and a producer of some of the finest silk cloth in the world, Bursa grew into a city of extraordinary wealth and the seed from which the Ottoman empire would flower.

caerphilly_desc.en: Home to the highest quality coal in Europe, the Welsh Valleys became a centre for iron-making in the latter half of the 18th century.
caerphilly_desc.uk: У валлійських долинах видобувалося найякісніше вугілля в Європі, завдяки чому в другій половині XVIII століття цей регіон став важливим центром виробництва заліза.

cairo_desc.en: Founded in 969 by the Fatimid general Jawhar al-Siqilli beside the ancient Roman fortress of Babylon, Al-Qāhirah, 'The Victorious', quickly supplanted Alexandria as the heart of Egypt. Under the Ayyubids and Mamluks it grew into the most populous city in the Islamic world, its markets and mosques drawing merchants, scholars, and pilgrims from across three continents. When the Mongols shattered Baghdad in 1258, Cairo stood as the uncontested capital of Islamic civilization, a city of extraordinary grandeur whose minarets rose above a river valley that had sustained human life since the dawn of history.

candia_desc.en: When the Fourth Crusade shattered the Byzantine Empire in 1204, Venice acquired Crete and made Candia its capital, transforming it over the following century into one of the most strategically important Venetian outposts in the eastern Mediterranean. The island's fertile plains fed Venetian fleets and colonies alike, and Candia's harbor served as a critical resupply point on the sea lanes between Venice and the Levant. Though the Cretan population rose in repeated rebellion against their Venetian lords, the city itself was steadily fortified and enriched, its walls and warehouses proclaiming a colonial power that intended to hold Crete indefinitely.

changsha_desc.en: Since its founding, the city center of Chángshā has remained unchanged for two thousand years.
changsha_desc.uk: З часів побудови місто Чанша протягом двох тисяч років залишалося головним економічним і адміністративним центром регіону.

cologne_desc.en: Founded as #italic Colonia Claudia Ara Agrippinensium#! by the Romans in AD 50, Cologne grew into the largest city in medieval Germany and one of the most powerful archbishoprics in the Holy Roman Empire. The magnificent Gothic cathedral, begun in 1248 to house the relics of the Three Kings, rose as a symbol of the city's ambition and faith. As a Free Imperial City and a founding member of the Hanseatic League, Cologne commanded the vital Rhine trade route and served as the gateway between the North Sea and the heart of the empire.

constantinople_desc.en: Crowned by Hagia Sophia and encircled by mighty walls, Constantinople stood as the heart of the Eastern Roman Empire. For a thousand years, its wealth and grandeur made it the envy of the world.
constantinople_desc.uk: Оточений могутніми стінами, Константинополь був серцем Східної Римської імперії і місцем розташування собору Святої Софії — одного з найбільших у світі храмів. Протягом тисячі років велич і багатство цього міста були предметом заздрощів для всього світу.

cordoba_desc.en: In its golden age Córdoba was the greatest city in western Europe, a city of half a million souls, of paved streets and public baths, of libraries that dwarfed anything Christendom could offer. Under Abd al-Rahman III, who declared himself Caliph in 929, it became the capital of a rival caliphate that challenged the Abbasids in Baghdad and the Carolingians in the north. Scholars such as Averroes and Maimonides walked its streets, and its Great Mosque, the #italic Mezquita#!, stood as a monument to the extraordinary civilization that had taken root on Iberian soil. The city's capture by Ferdinand III of Castile in 1236 brought this era to a close, but its legacy endured in the knowledge it had preserved and transmitted to the wider world.

corinth_desc.en: Commanding both the narrow land passage between mainland Greece and the Peloponnese and the ancient portage route across the Isthmus, Corinth was one of the wealthiest and most strategically vital cities of the ancient Greek world. In its heyday it controlled the trade between the Aegean and the Adriatic, levying tolls on goods dragged overland between its two harbors, and its bronzework and decorated pottery were exported to every corner of the Mediterranean. Though devastated by the Roman general Lucius Mummius in 146 BC, it was refounded by Julius Caesar as a Roman colony and endured as a major city, passing through Byzantine, Latin, and Frankish hands as successive powers recognized the commanding value of its position.

cremona_desc.en: Planted by the Romans on the south bank of the Po as a frontier colony in 218 BC, Cremona grew into one of the great cities of the Lombard plain, its position on the river making it a natural hub of road and water trade between east and west. The city became a byword for Ghibelline loyalty in the bitter wars between emperor and pope, suffering for its allegiances but also earning extraordinary imperial favor and wealth. Its skyline, dominated by the great #italic Torrazzo#!, the tallest medieval bell tower in Italy, and a forest of rival family towers, proclaimed the competitive civic pride of a city where power was displayed as fiercely as it was wielded.

dadu_desc.en: On the plains south of the Taihang Mountains, Kublai Khan raised Dàdū, 'Great Capital', as the seat of his Yuan dynasty in 1267, upon the ruins of the Jin dynasty's Zhōngdu. Marco Polo marveled at its grandeur, describing a city of broad avenues, vast palaces, and storehouses heaving with the wealth of all China. Even as Mongol power waned, the city's position at the northern gateway between the steppe and the Chinese heartland ensured its endurance as an imperial center.

damascus_desc.en: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, Damascus commands a fertile oasis at the foot of the Anti-Lebanon mountains, its markets fed by the waters of the Barada River. As the capital of the Umayyad Caliphate in the 7th and 8th centuries, it stood at the center of the largest empire the world had yet seen, its Great Mosque rising as one of the supreme achievements of Islamic architecture. Though the Abbasids shifted power to Baghdad, Damascus endured as one of the Levant's foremost commercial and cultural cities, its bazaars trading in silk, fine swords, and the fragrant roses for which it was famous.

delhi_desc.en: Situated on the western bank of the Yamuna, Delhi has served as a seat of power for successive dynasties since ancient times. The Slave Dynasty established the Delhi Sultanate here in 1206, and under rulers such as Iltutmish and Alauddin Khalji the city grew into the preeminent Islamic capital of South Asia. Its great mosques, markets, and fortresses drew scholars and merchants from across the Islamic world, cementing Delhi's place as the gateway through which much of the subcontinent was governed.

doncaster_desc.en: Once the Roman fort of Danum, by 1337 Doncaster had become a Yorkshire market town on the Great North Road, where rovers and traders carried goods between London and the north.
doncaster_desc.uk: Через Донкастер, відомий раніше під римською назвою Данум, проходила Велика північна дорога, якою мандрівники та торговці перевозили товари між Лондоном і північними землями. Завдяки такому вигідному розташуванню Донкастер до 1337 року став одним із найбагатших міст Йоркширу.

dubno_desc.en: Dubno, first noted in 1100, grew into a Volhynian trade hub renowned for its fairs and 1492 castle, later immortalized in Gogol's #italic Taras Bulba#!.
dubno_desc.uk: Місто Дубно, вперше згадане в 1100 році, було великим торговельним центром Волині, відомим своїми великими ярмарками. У 1492 році тут було зведено замок, навколо якого розгортаються події повісті Миколи Гоголя #italic «Тарас Бульба»#!.

dubrovnik_desc.en: Sheltered beneath the limestone cliffs of the Dalmatian coast, Dubrovnik grew from a Byzantine-founded refuge into one of the most prosperous and diplomatically adroit small states in the medieval Mediterranean. As the Republic of Ragusa, it navigated the competing pressures of Venice, Hungary, Serbia, and the emerging powers beyond with extraordinary skill, paying tribute where necessary while maintaining a network of merchant consulates that stretched from Flanders to the Levant. Its merchants carried goods and credit across the known world, and the elegant stone city rising behind its massive walls proclaimed a civilization that chose commerce and careful diplomacy over the costs of war.

dunstable_desc.en: Roman city to Priory town; famed for Henry I's royal house (1109), Eleanor's Cross (1290), Henry VIII's divorce (1533), and Cromwell's recruiting place (1642).
dunstable_desc.uk: Данстабл виник на місці стародавнього римського поселення. Вже в Середні віки англійці заснували тут монастир. За свою довгу історію місто пережило низку історичних подій. Зокрема, тут розлучився зі своєю дружиною Генріх VIII, а великий полководець Олівер Кромвель набирав у навколишніх землях добровольців для участі в громадянській війні. Крім того, тут розташована стара резиденція Генріха I і один із дванадцяти пам'ятних хрестів Елеонори.

durres_desc.en: One of the oldest cities in Europe, Durrës was founded as the Greek colony of Epidamnus around 627 BC by settlers from Corinth and Corfu, its fine natural harbor on the eastern Adriatic giving it immediate commercial importance. The Romans knew it as #italic Dyrrachium#! and made it the western terminus of the Via Egnatia, the great military road that crossed the Balkans to Byzantium, ensuring that for centuries every army marching from Rome to the east passed through its gates. Its position as the gateway between Italy and the Balkans made it one of the most fought-over cities in the region, its harbor and walls changing hands between Byzantines, Normans, Venetians, and Angevin lords across the medieval centuries.

edirne_desc.en: Founded by the Roman emperor Hadrian on the banks of the Maritsa River and named #italic Hadrianopolis#! in his honor, Adrianople guarded the main route between Constantinople and the Danube frontier and served as a key military and administrative center for the defense of Thrace. It was here in 378 that the Visigoth cavalry shattered the legions of Emperor Valens in one of antiquity's most consequential battles, a defeat that set in motion the accommodation of the Germanic peoples within the empire's borders and helped bring about the eventual collapse of the western Roman state. Under the Byzantines Adrianople remained the foremost city of Thrace and the traditional first line of defense for Constantinople against threats from the west.

erbach_desc.en: In the late 18th century, Erbach developed into a major center for ivory carving after Count Francis I of Erbach, driven by his passion for antiquities, financed a local ivory carving guild.
erbach_desc.uk: Наприкінці XVIII століття граф Франциск I, що живив великий інтерес до реліквій давнини, виділив кошти на створення в Ербасі гільдії різьбярів, яка займалася створенням виробів з слонової кістки. Завдяки цьому місто привабило численних творців і стало одним із головних центрів цього ремесла.

ferrara_desc.en: Rising at the edge of the Po delta marshlands, Ferrara developed from a modest river crossing into a city shaped by the ambitions of the Este dynasty, who established themselves as its lords in the 13th century. Under their long patronage the city became a center of chivalric culture and refined court life, its lords hosting poets, jousts, and scholarly debate while carefully navigating the rivalries of Milan, Venice, and the Papal States. The wide straight streets and imposing Este castle that defined Ferrara's character were emblematic of a city where order and elegance were as important as walls and soldiers.

florence_desc.en: Straddling the Arno in the heart of Tuscany, Florence grew from a Roman colony into a city of merchants and bankers who reshaped European commerce. The great banking houses, the Bardi, the Peruzzi, and the Strozzi, extended their credit across kingdoms, and the gold florin they minted became the standard currency of international trade. Wracked by the rivalry of #italic Guelfi#! and #italic Ghibellini#! and governed by its powerful guilds, Florence combined fierce civic pride with extraordinary wealth, laying the ground for the artistic and intellectual flowering that would soon make it the envy of the world.

gdansk_desc.en: Its name as first recorded in the year 997, City of Gdańsk, was born from a settlement which existed on the coast of the Baltic Sea. It became a major shipbuilding and trade port, cementing its position as one of the wealthiest and most influential cities in Eastern Europe.
gdansk_desc.uk: Перша письмова згадка про Гданськ відноситься до 997 року, проте поселення там існувало задовго до цього. В епоху пізнього Середньовіччя Гданськ перетворився на великий торговельний порт і центр суднобудування, завдяки чому він став одним із найбагатших і найвпливовіших міст Східної Європи.

genoa_desc.en: Sheltered behind the arc of the Ligurian Apennines, Genoa built its greatness entirely on the sea. Its merchants and admirals carved out a maritime empire of trading posts and colonies stretching from the Black Sea to the Atlantic, and its fleets clashed repeatedly with those of Venice for mastery of Mediterranean commerce. Driven by the relentless ambition of its great families, the Doria, the Grimaldi, and the Spinola, the republic earned its proud epithet #italic La Superba#! and proved that a city with almost no hinterland could nonetheless become one of the wealthiest powers in Christendom.

glasgow_desc.en: Glesca (Glasgow), founded as a Medieval bishopric, flourished around its great cathedral, gaining burgh status, and a university that shaped Scotland's learning.
glasgow_desc.uk: Глазго виник навколо середньовічного собору, який слугував резиденцією місцевого архиєпископства. У XV столітті тут було засновано університет, який посприяв становленню Глазго як освітнього центру Шотландії.

grenoble_desc.en: Grenoble is a modest but strategic town nestled in the French Alps, serving as the capital of the Dauphiné. Surrounded by rivers and mountains, it is protected by walls and dominated by the fortress of the Bastille. Life centers around the cathedral and narrow, winding streets filled with merchants, artisans, and peasants bringing goods from the surrounding valleys.
grenoble_desc.uk: Гренобль — невелике, але стратегічно важливе місто в Альпах, що є столицею провінції Дофіне. Оточене річками та горами, воно чудово підходить для оборони місцевих земель, у зв'язку з чим тут було зведено фортецю Бастилія. Навколо місцевого собору простягаються вузькі звивисті вулиці, де живуть і працюють купці, ремісники та селяни, що привозять сюди продукти із сусідніх долин.

grojec_desc.en: Up until the 12th century, it had been the seat of the local castellany and archdiocese of Poznań, but it gradually lost its importance in favor of the neighboring Czersk.
grojec_desc.uk: До XII століття в Груєці розташовувалася Познанська архиєпархія і резиденція місцевого каштеляна, проте у зв'язку із зростанням впливу сусіднього міста Черська він поступово втратив своє значення.

hangzhou_desc.en: Known in its heyday as #italic Kinsai#!, meaning 'temporary capital', Hangzhou served as the seat of the Southern Song dynasty after the north fell to the Jurchen Jin in 1127. Marco Polo, who visited in the late 13th century, called it the greatest city in the world, marveling at its canals, silk markets, and the great squares where goods of every description changed hands. Even after the Mongol conquest of 1279, its position at the head of the Grand Canal and its mastery of silk and porcelain trades ensured its survival as one of China's foremost commercial cities.

hanover_desc.en: Hanover rose from a medieval settlement to a key Holy Roman Empire city, ruled by the Welfs and thriving as a center of trade, power, and culture.
hanover_desc.uk: Зі скромного поселення Ганновер поступово перетворився на одне з ключових міст Священної Римської імперії. Під управлінням династії Вельфів місто стало розвиненим торговельним і культурним центром, який до того ж мав великий політичний вплив.

heidelberg_desc.en: In the late 12th century, Heidelberg became the seat of the Count Palatine of the Rhine and a renowned castle was constructed. Heidelberg is known for being home to the first German university and, therefore it has long been a center of learning. Afterwards, it became a center of reformation and tolerance with the Palatinate eventually becoming the leader of the Protestant Union. Later on, the castle and its iconic look attracted many poets to the city, which lead to it becoming a symbol of Romanticism, earning the city the nickname #italic City of Romanticism#!.
heidelberg_desc.uk: Наприкінці XII століття Гейдельберг став резиденцією пфальцграфа Рейнського, у зв'язку з чим тут було зведено вражаючий замок. Пізніше в цьому місті було засновано перший університет Німеччини, завдяки чому він став важливим науковим і освітнім центром. У ході Реформації Гейдельберг приєднався до протестантського руху, що вплинуло на створення Євангелічної унії на чолі з Пфальцем. В епоху романтизму образ Гейдельберзького замку приваб­ив до міста величезну кількість поетів, за рахунок чого воно навіть отримало прізвисько #italic «місто романтики»#!.

ioannina_desc.en: Set on a rocky peninsula jutting into the mountain lake of Pamvotis, Ioannina was the principal city of the Despotate of Epirus, the Greek successor state that emerged in northwestern Greece after the Fourth Crusade shattered Byzantine power in 1204. Under the Epirote despots it grew from a modest provincial town into a significant center of Greek culture and resistance, its natural defenses enhanced by strong walls and its lake providing both sustenance and protection. The mountain landscape of Epirus gave it security and isolation in equal measure, and Ioannina served as a vital stronghold anchoring Greek Christian civilization in the turbulent northwest of the former empire.

izmit_desc.en: Founded by the Bithynian king Nicomedes I in the 3rd century BC and known to the Romans as #italic Nicomedia#!, the city served as the eastern capital of the Roman Empire under Diocletian, who chose it as his personal residence and the administrative heart of the eastern provinces. It was from Nicomedia in 303 that Diocletian launched his Great Persecution of the Christians, tearing down the principal church within sight of the imperial palace and initiating the last and most severe Roman assault on the faith. After the foundation of Constantinople across the water it was gradually overshadowed by its great neighbor, but retained its importance as a major port and episcopal center throughout the Byzantine centuries.

jerusalem_desc.en: As the meeting point of faith and struggle, Jerusalem is revered by Jews, Christians, and Muslims alike. Pilgrims and conquerors continuously shape its sacred yet turbulent history.
jerusalem_desc.uk: Єрусалим є місцем перетину авраамічних релігій, а тому він має особливе значення для іудеїв, християн і мусульман. Історія та образ цього священного міста сформувалися під впливом численних завоювань і паломників, що прибувають сюди з усіх куточків світу.

jiaxing_desc.en: Jiāxīng is a border area between the Wú and Yuè regions. 'Jiā' means beauty and auspiciousness, while 'Xīng' stands for prosperity and thriving.
jiaxing_desc.uk: Цзясін розташований на кордоні між регіонами У та Юе. Слово «цзя» в його назві означає «краса», а «сін» — «процвітання».

kayseri_desc.en: Known to the Romans as #italic Caesarea Mazaca#!, the principal city of ancient Cappadocia, Kayseri served for centuries as the gateway between the Anatolian plateau and the routes leading east toward Armenia and Mesopotamia. One of the earliest centers of Christianity in Asia Minor, it was home to Saint Basil the Great, whose theological writings and monastic rule shaped the Eastern church and continue to influence Christian practice to this day. Under the Seljuks and their successors the city was enriched with mosques, madrasas, and caravanserais, its enduring position as a crossroads of Anatolian trade ensuring that it passed between Byzantine, Danishmendid, Seljuk, and Mongol hands as each master in turn recognized its value.

kendal_desc.en: Kendal was founded with a Roman fort on the bank of the River Kent in the 1st century AD. The town grew under Norman rule, gaining market rights in 1189 from King Richard I in exchange for money towards his crusading, which brought greater prosperity to the town. It became a medieval center for the wool trade and the main castle was owned by the Parr family, of which Catherine Parr, Queen consort to Henry VIII, is the most famous member.
kendal_desc.uk: Кендал було засновано на місці римського військового містечка, яке виникло на березі річки Кент ще в I столітті н.е. Поселення активно розвивалося за норманів: отримавши в 1189 році від короля Річарда I право на торгівлю в обмін на фінансову підтримку його хрестового походу, Кендал почав процвітати і з часом став важливим центром середньовічної торгівлі вовною. Головний замок міста належав родині Парр, найвідомішою представницею якої була Катерина — дружина короля Генріха VIII.

kinsale_desc.en: Kinsale is a small but lively port town on Ireland's southern coast, sheltered by its deep natural harbor. Fishing and coastal trade sustained much of its population, with merchants exchanging salted fish, hides, and wool for wine, salt, and luxury goods from Iberia and France. Narrow streets clustered around the quays, where local seafarers mingled with occasional foreign traders. Though modest in size, Kinsale's harbor made it strategically valuable, a gateway between Ireland and continental Europe.
kinsale_desc.uk: Кінсейл являв собою невелике, але вельми жваве портове містечко, розташоване в природній гавані на південному узбережжі Ірландії. Основними заняттями міщан були рибна ловля і торгівля. Так, місцеві купці обмінювали рибу, шкури та вовну на вино, сіль і предмети розкоші з Іберії та Франції. На вузьких вулицях навколо причалів подекуди зустрічалися іноземні торговці, з якими ірландські моряки обмінювалися історіями і укладали угоди. Попри скромні розміри гавані, саме вона дозволила Кінсейлу стати стратегічно важливим портовим містом, яке з'єднувало Ірландію з континентальною Європою.

kitchissippi_desc.en: Named after the Kichi Sibi river, here the Anishinaabe peoples hunted and traded until British settlement expanded the lumber trade, and later made it the seat of colonial administration.
kitchissippi_desc.uk: Це місто було названо на честь річки Кічисіпі, нині відомої як Оттава. На цих землях народ анішинабе займався полюванням і торгівлею, поки британські поселенці не розширили вирубку лісів і не заснували тут місто, що стало резиденцією їхньої колоніальної адміністрації.

konya_desc.en: Set on the high plateau of central Anatolia, Konya served as the capital of the Sultanate of Rum, the Turkish state that dominated Anatolia for much of the 12th and 13th centuries. Under the Seljuk sultans the city flourished as a center of Islamic art, architecture, and learning, its tiled mausoleums and madrasas transforming an ancient plateau city into one of the great cultural centers of the medieval Islamic world. It was here that the mystic poet Jalal al-Din Rumi settled and died, and here that his followers founded the Mevlevi order, the Whirling Dervishes, whose music and ceremony spread the city's name far beyond the Anatolian plateau.

krakow_desc.en: Starting as a hamlet on Wawel Hill, it was first mentioned by name in 965, described as a notable commercial center of its time. It became the seat of Polish monarchs from the Piast dynasty in 1038, and subsequently served as the center of administration, economy, and culture for the Kingdom of Poland.
krakow_desc.uk: Про поселення на Вавельському пагорбі було відомо ще в давнину, проте вперше Краків згадується в документі від 965 року, де він описується як великий торговельний город. У 1038 році Краків став резиденцією польських монархів з династії Пястів, і відтоді він слугував одним із головних адміністративних, економічних і культурних центрів Польського королівства.

kunow_desc.en: An important part of the estates of the Bishopric of Kraków, with a parish existing since 1281, its name probably comes from the marten (pol. 'kuna'), which was abundant in the forests covering these areas.
kunow_desc.uk: Кунув з раннього Середньовіччя перебував у віданні Краківської архиєпархії, проте парафія тут з'явилася лише в 1281 році. Своєю назвою місто, ймовірно, зобов'язане куницям, які в достатку водилися в навколишніх лісах.

kyoto_desc.en: When Emperor Kanmu moved the imperial court here in 794, naming it #italic Heian-kyō#!, meaning 'Capital of Peace and Tranquility', Kyoto became the heart of Japanese civilization for centuries. Its grid of broad avenues, lined with aristocratic estates and Buddhist temples, housed the most refined court culture in the world, producing the poetry, painting, and literature of the Heian period. Though civil war, fire, and the rise of the samurai repeatedly shook its walls, the city endured as the seat of the emperor and the cultural soul of Japan.

leipzig_desc.en: Founded in 1165 on the crossroad of the #italic Via Imperii#! and the #italic Via Regia#!, Leipzig grew into a wealthy trade hub. Later privileged with important imperial privileges, Leipzig and its trade are an important center for the fur trade and the developing book industry.
leipzig_desc.uk: Заснований у 1165 році на перетині #italic Імперської#! та #italic Царської#! доріг, Лейпциг досить швидко перетворився на багате й розвинене місто за рахунок торгівлі хутром. Отримавши низку значних привілеїв, він став важливим торговельним вузлом Європи та одним із центрів книгодрукування в регіоні.

leksand_desc.en: This village on the southern coast of Lake Siljan has been populated for several millennia. The Church was built in the early 12th century, and it is now most famous for their first lutheran minister being an ancestor of Johan.
leksand_desc.uk: Це містечко на південному березі озера Сільян існує вже понад тисячу років. У XII столітті тут було побудовано церкву, першим протестантським главою якої був далекий предок Юхана Андерссона — провідного гейм-дизайнера Europa Universalis V.

lisbon_desc.en: Occupying a natural harbor where the Tagus meets the Atlantic, Lisbon has sheltered sailors and merchants since Phoenician times. The Romans fortified it as #italic Olisipo#!, and in the 8th century its Moorish rulers transformed it into a prosperous city of mosques and palaces. After Alfonso I captured it in 1147 with the help of crusading knights, Lisbon became the capital of the nascent Kingdom of Portugal and a vital Atlantic port, its deep harbor and westward gaze already pointing toward the unexplored ocean beyond.

london_desc.en: Anchored on the Thames, London grew from Roman Londinium into England's foremost city. Its thriving trade and royal courts made it the kingdom's political and economic heart.
london_desc.uk: Побудований в гирлі річки Темзи, Лондон пройшов довгий шлях від невеликого римського поселення до найбільшого міста Англії. Нині тут зосереджена вся політична та економічна міць королівства.

lublin_desc.en: Lublin was founded as a settlement at the turn of the 12th and 13th centuries, and received its charter from Władysław 'the Elbow-high' in 1317. In the following centuries, the city became an important trading center, and in the 16th century, it experienced its golden age, growing richer thanks to the Union of Lublin and extensive trade, especially with the East.
lublin_desc.uk: Люблін було засновано на рубежі XII–XIII століть, а статус міста отримав від Владислава Локетека в 1317 році. У наступні століття Люблін перетворився на великий торговельний центр, розквіт якого припав на XVI століття. Саме в цей час було укладено Люблінську унію, яка й дозволила місту збагатитися за рахунок розвитку торгівлі зі Сходом.

lucca_desc.en: Enclosed within its ancient Roman street grid and surrounded by the rich silk-producing countryside of the Garfagnana, Lucca was one of the wealthiest cities of medieval Italy. Its merchants spread across Europe, their banking houses and silk trade making the name #italic Lucchese#! synonymous with fine cloth in the markets of Paris, London, and Bruges, while at home the city accumulated wealth enough to build one of the finest collections of Romanesque churches in Tuscany. Though repeatedly threatened by Pisa and Florence, Lucca clung to its independence with remarkable tenacity, its sturdy walls and fierce civic pride keeping it free long after rival cities had fallen to lordly rule.

malmo_desc.en: A key stronghold on the Øresund, Malmö commands the passage between the Baltic and the North Sea. Its fortified walls and vigilant defenders make it a center of power and a city shaped by strategy and ambition.
malmo_desc.uk: Мальме контролює прохід суден через протоку Ересунн, що з'єднує Балтійське та Північне море. У зв'язку з цим місто є найважливішим стратегічним пунктом, захист якого забезпечують його міцні стіни та пильний гарнізон.

manhattan_desc.en: Originally inhabited by the Lenape people, the island that they called Manhatta was bought by Dutch settlers for 60 guilders worth of trade goods. Here, they would build a fort, the seat of power for the city of New Amsterdam.
manhattan_desc.uk: Колись населений народом ленапе, острів Манна-хата було придбано голландськими поселенцями в обмін на товари загальною вартістю всього 60 гульденів. Тут вони збудували фортецю, яка стала центром влади Нового Амстердама.

mantova_desc.en: Ringed on three sides by the lakes formed by the slow Mincio River, Mantua occupies one of the most naturally defensible sites in northern Italy and has been inhabited since the Bronze Age. The Romans celebrated it as the birthplace of Virgil, the greatest of their poets, and the city's destiny has long been shaped by the artistic and literary ambitions of its rulers. By the early 14th century the Gonzaga family were rising to prominence here, and under their long patronage Mantua would grow into one of the most cultivated and refined courts in Italy.

megara_desc.en: Founded and inhabited since ancient times, Megara was ruled by legendary kings such as Nisos and Byzas. The city became a significant power in the Greek peninsula, renowned for its naval strength and thriving trade. Its colonists went on to establish important settlements across the Mediterranean, including Byzantion, Chersonesos, and Selinous. Over time, however, Megara gradually fell into obscurity, leaving behind only traces of its former prominence.
megara_desc.uk: У давнину Мегарою правив легендарний герой Ніс, а деякі її уродженці заснували в Середземномор'ї такі великі міста, як Візантіон, Херсонес і Селінунт. Надалі Мегара стала важливим торговельним центром і здобула величезний вплив на території Греції — багато в чому завдяки своєму потужному флоту. Однак відтоді вона втратила більшу частину своєї могутності, і нині від її колишньої величі залишилася лише тінь.

messina_desc.en: Commanding the narrow strait that separates Sicily from the Italian mainland, Messina was founded by Greek colonists who called it #italic Zankle#! for the curved sickle shape of its harbor, and its position made it from the first one of the Mediterranean's great strategic ports. It was through Messina that the Normans began their conquest of Sicily in 1061, and through its harbor that armies of every subsequent age, Angevin, Hohenstaufen, and crusaders bound for the Holy Land, passed between east and west. Though repeatedly shaken by earthquake and political upheaval, the city's extraordinary natural harbor ensured that it always recovered, drawing commerce and conflict in equal measure.

milano_desc.en: Rising at the heart of the Po plain, Milan's origins as a Celtic settlement were swept aside when the Romans made it #italic Mediolanum#!, for a time the de facto capital of the western empire. After the barbarian migrations reduced its grandeur the city revived as a free commune, repelling Frederick Barbarossa and his imperial armies at the Battle of Legnano in 1176. Under the Visconti family, who seized signorial power in the late 13th century, Milan became the seat of a lordship that steadily absorbed the surrounding cities of Lombardy, making it the dominant force in northern Italy.

moscow_desc.en: Founded as a minor wooden fort by Yuri Dolgoruky in 1147 on the banks of the Moskva River, Moscow long stood in the shadow of older Rus' cities. Yet under the Mongol yoke the Muscovite princes proved adept at survival and expansion, collecting tribute for the Golden Horde while quietly absorbing neighboring principalities. Its position at the crossroads of northern river routes gave it the commercial foothold from which it steadily grew, and by the early 14th century its grand prince wielded greater power than any other ruler in Rus'.

naples_desc.en: Founded as the Greek colony of Neapolis around 600 BC on the shores of its spectacular bay, the city passed through Roman, Byzantine, Norman, and Hohenstaufen hands before the Angevin dynasty made it the capital of the Kingdom of Naples in 1266. Under the Angevins it became one of the great royal courts of medieval Europe and the most populous city in Italy, its port channeling the wealth of the Mezzogiorno toward the wider world. The court at Naples attracted scholars, artists, and theologians, among them Thomas Aquinas, who taught and died here, making it a center of intellectual life as well as dynastic power.

neva_desc.en: The Neva delta, once part of the Varangian-Greek trade route, became Saint Petersburg in 1703 and remained Russia's capital for over 200 years.
neva_desc.uk: Санкт-Петербург було закладено в дельті річки Неви, яка колись була частиною варязько-грецького торговельного шляху. Засноване в 1703 році, це місто слугувало столицею Росії понад 200 років.

ningxiang_desc.en: The largest bronze #italic zūn#! (wine vessel) of the Shāng Dynasty (three thousand years ago) was unearthed in here.
ningxiang_desc.uk: У Нінсяні було знайдено найбільший бронзовий #italic цзунь#! (ритуальну посудину для вина), виготовлений понад 3000 років тому за часів правління династії Шан.

nis_desc.en: Known to the Romans as #italic Naissus#!, Niš commanded the main road between the Danube frontier and Constantinople at the point where the valleys of the Morava and Nišava rivers meet, making it one of the most strategically vital cities of the ancient Balkans. It was here, around 272 AD, that the Emperor Constantine the Great was born, a son of the western Balkans who would reshape the Roman Empire and the entire course of Western civilization. Though repeatedly devastated, by Attila the Hun among others, the city's crossroads position ensured its revival, and under Byzantine, Bulgarian, and Serbian rule it remained the key junction of the central Balkans.

novgorod_desc.en: Lord Novgorod the Great, as its citizens proudly called it, grew from a Viking trading post on the Volkhov River into the most powerful merchant republic of northern Europe. Its elected assembly, the #italic veche#!, governed with a democratic voice rarely heard elsewhere in the feudal world, and its Hanseatic trading partners carried Novgorodian furs, wax, and amber to markets from London to Lübeck. While other Rus' cities fell to the Mongol devastation of the 1230s, Novgorod's northern position spared it, leaving it the wealthiest and most independent city in all of Rus'.

ohrid_desc.en: Set on the shores of the ancient lake that bears its name, Ohrid rose to prominence when Saint Clement, a disciple of the missionaries Cyril and Methodius, established his great school of Slavic learning here in the late 9th century, training thousands of priests and scholars in the new Slavic literacy. After the conversion of Bulgaria, Ohrid became the seat of the Bulgarian Patriarchate and later the autocephalous Archbishopric of Ohrid, one of the most important religious centers in the Orthodox world. Its hillside crowded with churches and monasteries, the city earned the name the Jerusalem of the Balkans, its spiritual authority shaping the Christianity of the South Slavic peoples for centuries.

osnabruck_desc.en: Osnabrück, a Medieval trading hub in the Holy Roman Empire, gained renown as a bishopric and for hosting the Peace of Westphalia negotiations.
osnabruck_desc.uk: У Середні віки Оснабрюк слугував центром місцевого єпископства і важливим торговельним вузлом Священної Римської імперії. Серед іншого місто відоме тим, що в ньому було підписано одну з двох угод, які привели до укладення Вестфальського миру.

paderborn_desc.en: Bishopric founded around 800 AD, first meeting place of Charlemagne and Pope Leo III. Besieged 16 times in the Thirty Years' War. Devastated by Swedish troops in 1646.
paderborn_desc.uk: З моменту свого заснування близько 800 року Падерборн слугував центром місцевого єпископства. Саме тут уперше зустрілися Карл Великий і папа римський Лев III. За часів Тридцятилітньої війни місто зазнало великої шкоди: воно пережило 16 облог, останню з яких влаштувала шведська армія в 1646 році.

padova_desc.en: Founded in legend by the Trojan hero Antenor and flourishing as one of the wealthiest cities of Roman Italy, Padova grew in the Middle Ages into a prosperous commune at the heart of the Veneto. Its university, founded in 1222 by scholars who broke away from Bologna, swiftly became one of the foremost centers of law and medicine in Europe, drawing students from across the continent. In the early 14th century the great painter Giotto transformed the interior of its Arena Chapel into a landmark of Western art, while the city itself thrived under the rule of the Carrara family as a court of learning and ambition.

palermo_desc.en: Cradled between twin headlands on Sicily's northern coast, Palermo was founded by Phoenician traders and grew into a great city under Carthaginian and later Byzantine rule before the Arab conquest of the 9th century transformed it into a flourishing Islamic metropolis of mosques, gardens, and bazaars. The Norman kings who wrested it from Arab hands in 1072 built upon this cosmopolitan legacy with extraordinary results, fusing Arab, Byzantine, and Latin traditions into glittering royal chapels and palaces that proclaimed a civilization unlike any other in Christendom. As the capital of the Norman Kingdom of Sicily and later the Hohenstaufen Empire, Palermo became one of the most cultivated and powerful royal courts in the medieval world.

paris_desc.en: On the banks of the Seine, Paris rose from a modest settlement into the crown jewel of France. With its cathedral, markets, and schools, it became one of Europe's foremost centers of power and culture.
paris_desc.uk: Розташований на річці Сені, Париж поступово перетворився зі скромного поселення на справжню перлину Франції. Завдяки своєму знаменитому собору, великим ринкам і навчальним закладам він став одним із найважливіших політичних і культурних центрів Європи.

parma_desc.en: Founded by the Romans on the Via Emilia in 183 BC, Parma became one of the great cities of the Lombard plain, its position on the great road between Milan and Bologna and its fertile surrounding farmland making it a consistently prosperous and contested prize. As a free commune it was among the most vigorous members of the Lombard League against Frederick Barbarossa, and after years of bitter factional strife between Guelph and Ghibelline families it passed through the hands of successive signori. Its cathedral and baptistery, raised in the Romanesque style of the 12th century, expressed a civic piety and wealth that outlasted the political turbulence of its communal age.

pavia_desc.en: For two centuries after the fall of Rome, Pavia served as the capital of the Lombard kingdom in Italy, home to its warrior kings and custodian of their crown of iron. The Carolingian emperors maintained it as their Italian residence, and it retained its prestige as a royal and coronation city long after the Lombard realm had been absorbed into the Frankish empire. Its university, one of the oldest in Italy, was flourishing by the 9th century, and its position on the Ticino River commanding the western approach to the Po valley ensured that Pavia remained a prize contested by every power that sought to dominate the north.

penafiel_desc.en: #italic Penna Fidelis#!, 'Faithful Hill', was founded in the 10th century on the top of a hill that strategically controls the middle section of the Duero river valley, making it a hot spot in the border raid warfare against the Caliphate of Córdoba. Count Sancho García of Castile definitely fortified it and granted it a 'fuero' some time around 1013. Afterwards, it has grew into a rich town, due to its flourishing wine industry, ending up controlled by the powerful lineage of Don Juan Manuel.
penafiel_desc.uk: Місто Пеньяф'єль, чия назва походить від латинського #italic Pinna Fidelis#! («Вірна скеля»), було засновано в X столітті. Спочатку воно являло собою невеликий аванпост на вершині пагорба, призначений для відбиття набігів з боку Кордовського халіфату. Граф Санчо Гарсія значно укріпив його і в 1013 році надав йому фуерос — особливі міські права та привілеї. Згодом Пеньяф'єль перейшов у володіння впливового дона Хуана Мануеля і став вельми багатим містом із процвітаючою винороб­ною промисловістю.

perugia_desc.en: Perched on a hill commanding the upper Tiber valley, Perugia was one of the twelve cities of ancient Etruria and later a prosperous Roman municipality before it emerged in the Middle Ages as one of the most formidable and turbulent independent communes of central Italy. Its great Palazzo dei Priori and the Fontana Maggiore, completed in 1278 with sculpture by Nicola and Giovanni Pisano, expressed a civic pride and artistic ambition that rivaled anything in Tuscany. The university founded here in 1308 confirmed Perugia's determination to match its military and political power with an equal reputation for learning.

pingjin_desc.en: Tàiyuán, home to the holy site of Jìn Temple, has been one of the most important cities in Shānxī and northern China since the 5th century BC. In 979, Emperor Tàizōng of Sòng ordered the ancient city of Jìnyáng to be flooded and destroyed upon the conquest of Northern Hàn, and then renamed it the County of Píngjìn (lit. 'Pacification of Shānxī'), a disaster from which the city took a long time to recover.
pingjin_desc.uk: Тайюань, де розташований священний храм Цзінь, ще з V століття до н.е. є одним із найважливіших міст Шаньсі й усього Північного Китаю. У 979 році, під час завоювання Північної Хань, імператор Тай-цзун наказав затопити і знищити місто. На знак тріумфу і приниження своїх ворогів він перейменував захоплений регіон на Пінцзінь, що означає «замирення Шаньсі». Внаслідок затоплення від міста залишилися лише руїни, і на його відновлення пішли багато десятиліть.

pisa_desc.en: At the mouth of the Arno, Pisa built one of the great maritime empires of the medieval Mediterranean, its fleets raiding Palermo in 1063, defeating Saracen corsairs across the Tyrrhenian Sea, and establishing trading colonies from Sardinia to Antioch. Enriched by this commerce, the Pisans raised the extraordinary ensemble of cathedral, baptistery, and campanile on the #italic Campo dei Miracoli#!, monuments to a city whose wealth and confidence at its 12th-century height seemed without limit. Though the catastrophic defeat by Genoa at the Battle of Meloria in 1284 broke Pisan naval power, the city and its remarkable monuments endured.

porto_desc.en: Called the #italic Cidade Invicta#!, or 'Unvanquished City', it gave Portugal its name and made the Port wine of the Douro celebrated far beyond its shores.
porto_desc.uk: Саме від #italic «непереможного міста»#! Порту походить назва Португалії і знаменитого на весь світ портвейну, що виготовляється в долині річки Дору.

prague_desc.en: Perched above a bend in the Vltava River, Prague grew from a Slavic ford-settlement into one of the great cities of medieval Europe. The Přemyslid dynasty erected its castle and cathedral on the rocky promontory of Hradčany, and a thriving merchant town took root beneath it. As the seat of the Bohemian kings and a natural crossroads between eastern and western Europe, Prague drew German and Jewish merchants, craftsmen, and scholars, becoming by the early 14th century one of the most populous and prosperous cities north of the Alps.

prizren_desc.en: Nestled in a fertile valley below the peaks of the Šar Mountains, Prizren was a city of ancient foundation that the medieval Serbian state transformed into one of its principal centers from the 13th century onward. Under the Nemanjić dynasty it grew into a major administrative and commercial city, its Orthodox churches and monasteries expressing the piety and ambition of Serbian rulers who saw themselves as the heirs of Byzantine civilization. By the early 14th century it was one of the most important cities in the Serbian realm, its markets drawing merchants from Dubrovnik, Venice, and across the Levant to trade in the precious metals mined from the surrounding mountains.

radom_desc.en: A city expanded by the last Piast King Casimir III The Great, it remained an important political site throughout late Middle Ages and Renaissance. The city also hosted the signing of the Pact of Vilnius and Radom in 1401, and the #italic Nihil Novi#! act approval in 1505, during a parliament session in the royal castle.
radom_desc.uk: Після свого розширення і оновлення королем Казимиром III місто Радом стало важливим політичним центром Польщі, яким воно залишалося аж до кінця епохи Відродження. Саме тут у 1401 році було укладено Віленсько-Радомську унію, і тут же на сеймі 1505 року було прийнято закон #italic Nihil novi#!.

ravenna_desc.en: For a brief but extraordinary century Ravenna served as the last capital of the Western Roman Empire, and when Rome fell in 476 it was here that the courts of Odoacer and then the Ostrogothic king Theodoric upheld the forms and traditions of Roman governance. The Byzantine reconquest of the 6th century made it the western outpost of Constantinople, seat of the Exarchate of Ravenna, and it was during this era of Greek imperial rule that its craftsmen produced the astonishing mosaic cycles that fill its churches and mausoleums. Though long since overshadowed by Bologna and the growing cities of the Po valley, Ravenna retained in its extraordinary art the memory of an imperial glory found nowhere else in the Latin west.

rodos_desc.en: For much of antiquity Rhodes was the wealthiest and most cosmopolitan port in the eastern Mediterranean, its legendary Colossus, one of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world, once standing at the harbor entrance, and its maritime law, the #italic Lex Rhodia#!, governing commerce across the known sea. After centuries of Roman, Byzantine, and Arab influence the island passed to the Knights Hospitaller in 1309, who fortified it into one of the most powerful Christian strongholds in the eastern Mediterranean. Behind its massive walls the Knights transformed Rhodes into a center of crusading power, its galley fleets patrolling the sea lanes between Christendom and the Islamic east.

rome_desc.en: The Eternal City on the Tiber ruled an empire that spanned continents. Even after the fall of its Empire, Rome endured as a beacon of faith and authority, home to the Papacy.
rome_desc.uk: Колись Рим був центром могутньої імперії, яка простягалася на кілька континентів. Втім, навіть після її падіння Вічне місто змогло зберегти своє політичне і релігійне значення, ставши столицею Папської держави.

saint_marceilin_desc.en: Founded in the XIth c. Saint-Marcellin was the Dauphin's Council siege between 1337 and 1340. It became famous for its soft cheese with bloomy rind, served to Louis XI in 1461.
saint_marceilin_desc.uk: Заснований в XI столітті, Сен-Марселлен слугував резиденцією ради дофіна в період з 1337 по 1340 рік. Це місто також славиться своїм м'яким сиром із зморшкуватою скоринкою, який подавали при королівському дворі щонайменше з 1461 року.

salerno_desc.en: Nestled between the sea and the mountains of the Amalfi coast on its sheltered gulf, Salerno was chosen by the Norman conqueror Robert Guiscard as his capital after seizing it in 1076, serving as the first seat of Norman power in southern Italy before the royal court moved to Palermo. The city is most renowned for its #italic Schola Medica Salernitana#!, the oldest medical school in Europe, which flourished from the 9th century onward by drawing together the Greek, Arab, and Latin medical traditions that converged on this cosmopolitan southern shore. Physicians trained at Salerno spread across the continent, and the school's texts on anatomy, surgery, and herbal medicine shaped the practice of medicine throughout the medieval world.

samarkand_desc.en: One of the oldest cities in Central Asia, Samarkand sat astride the Silk Road where caravans bearing silk, spices, and ideas passed between China and the Mediterranean. Under the Samanids and Karakhanids it flourished as a major Islamic center of scholarship and craftsmanship, its artisans renowned across the known world for fine metalwork and paper. Though devastated by Genghis Khan's armies in 1220, the city's position on the great trade routes ensured its revival, its bazaars and workshops once more drawing the commerce of half the world.

sevilla_desc.en: Straddling the Guadalquivir on the fertile plains of Andalusia, Seville was one of the jewels of Moorish Spain. Under the Umayyads and later the Almohads it flourished as a center of culture, science, and trade, its great mosque rising beside the river as a testament to Islamic civilization's reach in Iberia. Reconquered by Ferdinand III of Castile in 1248, the city retained its cosmopolitan character and grew into the wealthiest city of Christian Spain, its river port channeling the riches of Andalusia toward the wider world.

siena_desc.en: Built on three hills in the heart of Tuscany, Siena was one of the great powers of medieval Italy, its wealth founded on the banking and wool trades that made the Sienese merchant families creditors to kings and popes alike. The city's fierce rivalry with Florence, barely fifty kilometers to the north, shaped the history of both for generations, while its great central piazza, the Campo, served as the stage for the civic life and political drama of one of Italy's proudest communes. The paintings of Duccio di Buoninsegna and the Lorenzetti brothers made Siena one of the foremost centers of Gothic art in Europe.

sitges_desc.en: In the Middle Ages, a Castle was built on the hill where the City Hall now stands. The first owner was the Bishopric of Barcelona, but in the 12th century it came under the ownership of the family which it is named after.
sitges_desc.uk: У Середні віки на пагорбі, де сьогодні розташована будівля муніципалітету, було побудовано замок. Спочатку він належав архиєпархії Барселони, проте в XII столітті перейшов до сім'ї, на честь якої й отримав свою назву.

sivas_desc.en: Commanding the high plateau where the main routes between Anatolia and Persia converge, Sivas was one of the great crossroads cities of the medieval Near East. Under the Sultanate of Rum it grew into a major provincial capital of extraordinary architectural ambition, and the great madrasas of the 13th century, among them the celebrated Gök Medrese and the Çifte Minareli, rank among the finest examples of Seljuk stonework in Anatolia. After the Mongol conquest the city served as a key administrative center for the Ilkhanate's Anatolian provinces, its markets and caravanserais channeling the long-distance trade that flowed between Central Asia and the Mediterranean.

smyrna_desc.en: One of the ancient cities of the Aegean coast, Smyrna was among the sites that claimed the honor of Homer's birth and later became one of the Seven Churches of Asia Minor addressed in the Book of Revelation. Under Byzantine rule it served as a major port linking the rich Anatolian hinterland to Aegean commerce, its harbor frequented by Venetian and Genoese merchants who established trading colonies along its wharves. In the late 13th and early 14th centuries the city passed between Byzantine, Genoese, and Aydinid Turkish hands in quick succession, its exceptional position making it a prize that no power in the Aegean could afford to ignore.

sredets_desc.en: Known to the Romans as #italic Serdica#!, the chief city of the province of Dacia Mediterranea, the city that would become Sofia had already witnessed centuries of history when the Bulgarians made it a provincial center of their empire. It was in Serdica that the Emperor Constantine convened the great Council of 343, one of the major synods of early Christianity, and it was reportedly here that he first considered planting his new imperial capital before choosing the site on the Bosphorus. Under the Byzantine and Bulgarian empires it served as a key crossroads where the main routes of the Balkans converge, its position at the foot of the Vitosha mountain ensuring it endured every conquest as a prize worth holding.

stockholm_desc.en: This town was founded in 1252 by Birger Jarl, on a location that was strategically chosen where Lake Mälaren meets the Baltic Sea. This allowed Stockholm to serve as both a fortress controlling access to the lake and a trading hub connecting inland Sweden to Hanseatic and Baltic trade networks.
stockholm_desc.uk: Стокгольм було засновано у 1252 році Біргером Магнуссоном у районі, де озеро Меларен впадає в Балтійське море. Завдяки своєму стратегічному розташуванню місто не лише контролювало доступ до озера, а й слугувало важливим торговельним вузлом, що пов'язував Швецію з купецькими мережами Ганзи в Балтиці.

stockton_desc.en: Stockton is an Anglo Saxon Settlement on the north bank of the River Tees, and was poorly populated until the Bishop freed the boroughs serfs, which made it attractive for craftsmen to move into. It became an important market for exporting wool and importing wine, though it would not gain any significant population until the Industrial Revolution.
stockton_desc.uk: Стоктон — англосаксонське поселення на північному березі річки Тіс. Воно залишалося вельми малонаселеним до тих пір, поки єпископ не звільнив місцевих кріпаків, що привабило сюди численних купців і ремісників. За рахунок цього Стоктон став важливим торговельним містом, яке займалося продажем місцевої вовни та ввезенням іноземних вин. Однак по-справжньому великим містом Стоктон став лише після промислової революції.

syracuse_desc.en: Founded by Corinthian settlers in 734 BC on a small island at the mouth of a great harbor, Syracuse grew into the mightiest Greek city of the western Mediterranean, its power underscored by the catastrophic defeat it inflicted on the Athenian expedition of 415 to 413 BC. It was here that Archimedes devised his legendary war machines with which the city held Roman armies at bay, and here that successive conquerors, Carthaginian, Roman, Byzantine, Arab, and Norman, each recognized a harbor too valuable to leave unoccupied. Though long since overshadowed by Palermo, Syracuse endured as the greatest city of southeastern Sicily, its ancient harbor and stone-cut streets still bearing witness to a civilization whose brilliance had shaped the whole of the ancient Mediterranean world.

tarnovo_desc.en: Perched on three hills above a bend of the Yantra River, Tarnovo was chosen as the seat of the Second Bulgarian Empire when the brothers Asen and Peter led their great rebellion against Byzantine rule in 1185. Under the Asen dynasty it grew into one of the most formidable fortified cities in the Balkans, its Tsarevets Hill crowned by the royal palace and the Patriarchal Cathedral, symbols of a state that at its 13th-century height extended from the Danube to the Aegean. After the empire's weakening under Mongol pressure, Tarnovo endured as the capital of a diminished but proud Bulgaria, its walls and imperial memory defining the city's identity far into the 14th century.

tenochtitlan_desc.en: Around 1325, following the legend that their god Huitzilopochtli had promised them an island where an eagle perched upon a cactus, the Mexica people founded Tenochtitlan on a marshy island in Lake Texcoco. Built on a site that offered both natural defense and access to the rich resources of the valley's surrounding shores, the young settlement grew with remarkable speed. Its causeways, raised gardens, and warrior traditions would one day make it the greatest city in the Americas and the heart of a formidable empire.

thessaloniki_desc.en: Long regarded as the second city of the Byzantine Empire after Constantinople, Thessaloniki's wealth and prestige stem from her strategic position in commerce. Her bustling ports channel valuable goods between Italy and the Roman heartland, serving as a vital bridge between East and West.
thessaloniki_desc.uk: Довгий час Фессалоніки вважалися другим за значенням містом Візантії після Константинополя. Своїм багатством вони зобов'язані вигідному розташуванню поблизу Егейського моря, що сприяє розвитку торгівлі. При цьому місцеві порти служать своєрідним мостом між Заходом і Сходом, дозволяючи перевозити товари між імперськими володіннями та Італією.

timbuktu_desc.en: Rising from the edge of the Sahara at a bend of the Niger River, Timbuktu grew from a seasonal Tuareg camp into one of the great cities of medieval Africa. Under the Mali Empire it became a crossroads of trans-Saharan trade, where caravans carrying salt from the north met gold and ivory traveling from the south. Its mosques and #italic madrasas#! drew Islamic scholars from across the continent, making it a city of learning whose libraries held tens of thousands of manuscripts on theology, mathematics, and astronomy.

torgau_desc.en: In 1452, Elector Frederick II established the first bear pit in Torgau, which was steadily enlarged until 1624. It provided space for up to 39 bears.
torgau_desc.uk: У 1452 році курфюрст Фрідріх II наказав створити біля замку в Торгау рів із ведмедем. Рів поступово розширювався аж до 1624 року, і в якийсь момент він міг вміщувати до 39 ведмедів одночасно.

toro_desc.en: Toro was founded in the 10th century as part of the efforts made by the Kings of León to fortify the border of the kingdom at the Duero river valley, in their fight against the Caliphate of Córdoba. It developed later as an important town, due to its strategic position, and its rich farming fields and vineyards.
toro_desc.uk: Торо було засновано в X столітті в долині річки Дуеро для захисту володінь Королівства Леон від військ Кордовського халіфату. Завдяки своєму вигідному розташуванню місто слугувало важливим оборонним вузлом, а теплий клімат і родючі землі дозволили йому також стати великим центром виноробства.

trebizond_desc.en: Perched on a narrow coastal shelf between the Pontic mountains and the Black Sea, Trebizond was one of the most dramatically situated cities in the medieval world. When Constantinople fell to the Fourth Crusade in 1204, members of the Komnenian dynasty fled here and founded the Empire of Trebizond, which endured as an independent Greek Christian state long after the Latin Empire had itself collapsed. Commanding the eastern end of the Black Sea trade route and the mountain passes into Armenia and Persia, the city attracted Genoese merchants and became a prosperous western terminus of the Silk Road, its markets drawing goods from Central Asia and beyond.

tunis_desc.en: First founded as Carthage by the legendary Queen Dido in year 814 BC, it became the capital of the Punic nation of the same name, being destroyed and later rebuilt by the Romans after three bloody wars. The modern city of Tunis was founded by the Arabs in 698 at the outskirts of these ancient ruins. The Almohad conquest in the 12th century saw its elevation to regional capital, status that was consolidated by the Hafsid dynasty.
tunis_desc.uk: Заснований легендарною цариною Дідоною в 814 році до н.е., спочатку це місто носило назву Карфаген і було столицею однойменної пунічної держави. Внаслідок трьох великих воєн воно було зруйноване, а потім заново відбудоване римлянами. Сучасне місто Туніс було закладено арабами в 698 році неподалік від стародавніх карфагенських руїн. Після завоювання Альмохадів у XII столітті місто фактично стало регіональною столицею, і під час правління династії Хафсідів цей статус лише зміцнився.

valladolid_desc.en: Founded in the last decades of the 11th century by counts Pedro Ansúrez and Eylo Alfonso near by a bridge over the river Pisuerga, Valladolid developed as a commercial town in the very center of the Northern Meseta. By the 14th century, it had become the most important city of the region, along with Burgos, and the main administrative center during the regencies of Queen María de Molina, and the reign of her grandson, King Alfonso XI.
valladolid_desc.uk: Вальядолід було засновано наприкінці XI століття графом Педро Ансуресом і його дружиною Ейло Альфонсо в самому центрі Північної Месети, поблизу річки Пісуерга. Завдяки торгівлі Вальядолід швидко став одним із найважливіших міст у регіоні поряд із Бургосом. До XIV століття він здобув настільки значний вплив, що слугував адміністративним центром держави при регенті Марії де Моліна та її онукові Альфонсо XI.

venice_desc.en: Rising from the mudflats of the Adriatic lagoon, Venice was shaped by necessity into ambition. Refugees fleeing Lombard invasions first sheltered on its islands, and by the 9th century the city had grown into a maritime republic governed by its elected Doge. From its Arsenal and counting houses, Venetian merchants commanded trade routes stretching from the Black Sea to the Levant, making Venice the wealthiest city in Christendom and the undisputed master of Mediterranean commerce.

verona_desc.en: Straddling the Adige at the southern edge of the Alps, Verona has been a place of passage since antiquity, its great Roman amphitheater, one of the largest and best preserved in the world, still rising above streets where legions and merchants once moved in equal measure. Under the della Scala family, the Scaligeri, who seized power in the late 13th century, it became one of the strongest signorie of northern Italy, its lords dominating the Veneto and projecting their reach toward the Adriatic. Among those who found refuge at the Scaligeri court was Dante Alighieri, completing his #italic Commedia#! under the patronage of Can Grande della Scala during his long years of Florentine exile.

vienna_desc.en: The Romans called it #italic Vindobona#!, planting a legionary fortress on the Danube to guard the empire's northern frontier. After the migration of peoples swept away the Roman order, it reemerged as the seat of the Babenberg margraves, who raised a city worthy of their ambitions on the same strategic ground. When the Habsburgs supplanted the Babenbergs in 1278, Vienna became the anchor of a dynastic empire, its position at the crossroads of the Danube valley making it one of the most strategically coveted cities in the Holy Roman Empire.

vijayanagar_desc.en: Founded in 1336 on the southern bank of the Tungabhadra River by the brothers Harihara and Bukka Raya, Vijayanagar, 'City of Victory', was raised as a bulwark of Hindu civilization against the expanding power of the Delhi Sultanate. Protected by the Tungabhadra and its forbidding landscape of granite boulders and rocky gorges, the fledgling capital already commanded the fertile plains of the central Deccan. From this rocky stronghold an empire would grow that endured for more than two centuries, its markets drawing traders and goods from across the Indian Ocean world.

warsaw_desc.en: Originating as a small fishing town in Mazovia, the city became prominent after the capital was moved there from Krakow by Sigismund III in 1596. Since then it continued growing becoming the largest Polish city in the 18th century. In that same century, it saw extensive development, contributing towards Polish architectural and artisanal scene.
warsaw_desc.uk: На зорі своєї історії Варшава являла собою невелике мазовецьке рибальське поселення. У 1596 році Сигізмунд III переніс столицю з Кракова до Варшави, після чого вона почала стрімко зростати і вже до XVIII століття стала найбільшим містом Польщі. У цей же час тут перебудували та звели численні будівлі, що значно посприяло розвитку польської архітектури і різноманітних ремесел.

wieliczka_desc.en: The town of Wieliczka was founded in 1290 by King Przemysł II of Poland, owing to the local extraction of salt deposits. A main mining town, it was granted many privileges and the local salt mine soon rose to prominence. The Wieliczka Salt Mine and its sister-mine in Bochnia became part of the #italic Żupy Krakowskie#! mining company. In formal documents, the town is known as #italic Wielka Sól#!, meaning #italic Great Salt#!.
wieliczka_desc.uk: Велічка було засновано в 1290 році Пшемислом II у районі соляних рудників. Видобуток цього цінного продукту приносив Польщі величезний прибуток, у зв'язку з чим місто отримало численні привілеї і стало великим промисловим центром. Так, шахти у Велічці та сусідній Бохні стали частиною соледобувної компанії #italic «Краківські жупи»#!, яка забезпечувала їх роботу до кінця XX століття. В офіційних документах за містом довгий час зберігалася його стара назва #italic Wielka Sól#!, що означає #italic «велика сіль»#!.

wurzburg_desc.en: Würzburg rose as a Franconian stronghold, becoming a bishopric in 741. It flourished around its fortress and Main River trade routes in the early Middle Ages.
wurzburg_desc.uk: Вюрцбург було утворено на місці франконської фортеці в 741 році, коли поселення, що там знаходилося, отримало статус єпископства. У ранньому Середньовіччі місто процвітало головним чином за рахунок свого вигідного розташування на річці Майн, якою проходили багато торговельних маршрутів.
